\begin{minipage}{0.95\linewidth}\vspace{4pt}\scriptsize \textit{Notes:} Countries whose general government reporting year does not start in January according to the IMF World Economic Outlook database (October 2026, attribute 'start/end months of reporting year' of general government expenditure); in the Table 1 sample: EGY, HKG, IRN, LSO, MUS, NPL, RWA, SGP, THA. Whether the GFS wage bill of these countries is converted to calendar years is not reported in the GFS metadata and could not be verified. Excluded: Table 1 (annual and five-year rows, their models and controls) and T3 re-estimated without these countries. Realigned: for fiscal years starting between April and September (EGY, HKG, IRN, LSO, MUS, NPL, RWA, SGP), the calendar-year ratio is the month-weighted average of the two fiscal years that overlap the calendar year, assuming each fiscal year is labelled by the calendar year that holds most of its months; measures over trend GDP and five-year measures are recomputed from the realigned ratio. Annual rows: Driscoll-Kraay standard errors; five-year rows: standard errors clustered by country. Differences: measures (or full and restricted samples) stacked with measure- or sample-specific fixed effects, controls and year effects; wild cluster bootstrap by country (Webb weights, 9,999 replications). Exploratory (post-plan, pre-registered in the second plan addendum). * p<0.10, ** p<0.05, *** p<0.01.\end{minipage}
